terms.comment: Hebrew for “praise the Lord”, sung in East and West alike. The Latin rite leaves it out in Lent; the Byzantine rite sings it at Lenten Matins in place of “God is the Lord”.

phrases.english: Let everything that breathes praise the Lord! Alleluia.

phrases.latin: hīs sūmptīs Daniēlus excitāvit in caelum faciem, cibōque fortis āmēn reddidit, alleluja dīxit
phrases.english: when he had eaten, Daniel lifted his face to heaven and, strong with the food, said amen and alleluia

alleluja.against: Lewis & Short allēlūja, after Greek ἀλληλούϊα
alleluja.html: Prud. Cath. 4.72, āmēn reddidit, alleluja dīxit: in the hendecasyllable the second syllable is light, as Lewis & Short note themselves (also Sid. Ep. 2.10). Hebrew הַלְלוּ־יָהּ has only a murmured vowel there. The u before consonantal j takes no macron, the syllable being heavy by position.
